subject: general
question: Presently, which of the following countries is NOT a beneficiary of India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Angola**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme was introduced by the Government of India in 2008.
 
• The scheme aims to provide market access at zero duty to products originating from Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
 
• Rwanda, Burundi, and Myanmar are some of the beneficiaries of the DFTP Scheme.
 
• Angola is currently not a beneficiary of India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme**

 
 
• The DFTP Scheme was launched by India to provide preferential market access for goods originating from Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
 
• The main objective is to enhance South-South cooperation and contribute to the development of LDCs.
 
• The scheme covers around 98% of tariff lines, making a wide range of products from LDCs eligible for zero-duty benefits.
 
• It has the potential to significantly boost exports from LDCs to India, thereby supporting their economic growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Least Developed Countries (LDCs)**
 
 
• LDCs are a group of countries that are recognized by the United Nations as being the most disadvantaged in terms of their low gross national income, weak human assets, and economic vulnerability.
 
• As of October 2023, there are 46 countries classified as LDCs.
 
• LDCs benefit from various international support measures, including preferential market access and development assistance.
 
• The aim is to help these countries overcome structural challenges, eradicate poverty, and achieve sustainable development.
